findings.title: OS Command Injection via Ping Tool — Output Parser Trick to Exfiltrate Flag
findings.description: The /ping endpoint executes user-supplied input via shell=True subprocess. The application parses ping output with a regex pattern '(.*?) packets transmitted, (.*?) received, (.*?)% packet loss'. An attacker can inject a semicolon-delimited shell command (e.g., INVALID; echo `cat /FLAG.txt` packets transmitted, 0 received, 0% packet loss) using backtick command substitution to craft output matching the regex. The parser then extracts and displays the injected command output (flag file contents) as the 'Packets Transmitted' value. Input validation blocks $() and >&1 but backtick substitution is allowed.
